text:
rachel: FYI found a staging proxy printing a service-account token during an automated batch run. grabbed sample logs and flagged it to sec.
sec-bot: Security detector: potential credential exposure (rule: token-in-logs). Created incident INC-2026-045. Priority: P2. https://incidents.internal/redwood/INC-2026-045
rachel: snippet from logs:
  \"2026-03-19T16:12:03Z proxy[batch-run]: DEBUG auth: got token=ya29.STAGING_PRINTOUT_EXAMPLE_ABC123; using svc acct\"
maya: Ugh. Which service account? can you paste full line and commit that introduced this? we need to rotate asap.
tom: If it's an SA key, disable/delete immediately then issue a new key. I'll stand up a short rotation window. oncall-ops, can you run usage checks for that token?
oncall-ops: Running gcloud logging read \"textPayload:~\"STAGING_PRINTOUT_EXAMPLE_ABC123\"\" --project=staging-project --limit=50. Also grepping batch-run logs on staging nodes.
rachel: commit that introduced the debug: https://git.internal/redwood/proxy/commit/3f9a2d6 (accidental debug left behind). Line: logger.debug(\"auth: got token=%s\", token)
maya: Plan: 1) disable the exposed key 2) rotate creds in Secret Manager 3) deploy proxy rollback or hotfix to remove debug 4) search for misuse and scope-check 5) notify CS if any customer impact
sara-cs: I'll check if any customer tokens were affected or if customers reported auth failures. so far no external incidents in last hour.
ton: Commands I'll run now:
  # list keys
  gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=ingest-staging@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=staging-project
  # delete compromised key (replace KEY_ID)
  gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete KEY_ID --iam-account=ingest-staging@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=staging-project
maya: After delete, push rotated secret: 
  gcloud secrets versions add projects/staging-project/secrets/ingest-staging-token --data-file=- < new-key.json
  kubectl set env deployment/proxy PROXY_SA_KEY=@secret:ingest-staging-token -n staging
sec-bot: Reminder: follow runbook -> https://runbooks.internal/security/token-leak. Postmortem checklist created in INC-2026-045. Also enable audit log export for the SA in question.
oncall-ops: Quick findings: two internal ingestion jobs used the token (timestamps match). No external IPs seen calling staging endpoints with it. No S3 or cloud-storage access anomalies yet.
rachel: Good catch. Let's also add a preventive guard: lint rule to block commits that log strings matching token regex and CI check to fail on debug prints of auth.*tokens.
maya: Agree. I'll open a PR to add a pre-commit grep and an Ops policy to deny logging of secrets. Also proposing KMS-sealed token format so raw tokens aren't present in runtime env vars.
sara-cs: I'll prepare a short CS note: \"no customer data exposed; internal staging token rotated; monitoring in place\" — will wait for final confirmation before sending.
ton: Deleted the key and created KEY_ID=abcd-rotated-01. Deployed rotated secret to staging. Proxy hotfix rolled (reverted debug commit). CI test added to block debug auth logs (initial rule pushed to staging branch).
rachel: Running final sweep of logs for any reuse. If we see calls after rotation, escalate. otherwise closing incident with follow-ups: PR for pre-commit, KMS plan, audit export retention increase.
sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 status: mitigated -> postmortem scheduled. Assignee: rachel + maya. Link: https://incidents.internal/redwood/INC-2026-045/postmortem
rachel: All done from my side. Token rotated, hotfix deployed, CS note queued. Will draft post-incident writeup tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
